title: Students' Perceived Roles, Opportunities, and Challenges of a Generative AI-powered Teachable Agent: A Case of Middle School Math Class
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how middle school students perceive the roles, benefits, and challenges of using a generative AI-powered teachable agent (TA) in mathematics learning. Rather than testing learning outcomes against a comparison condition, the study focuses on students’ lived experiences and perceptions of an AI system designed around learning-by-teaching principles.

The intervention was a GenAI-powered TA called [ANONYMOUS], built with GPT-4-Turbo and additional design features such as personalized topic/difficulty selection, contrast cases, gamification, and retrieval-augmented generation from math Q&A data. Students interacted with the TA through a chatbot-like interface by solving rate-and-ratio math problems and explaining fixes to the agent’s mistakes. The study was conducted with 108 sixth-grade students from six classes in a public laboratory research middle school in the Southeastern United States. Data came from classroom observations, open-ended surveys, and focus-group interviews.

Findings suggest that students saw the TA as a learning companion, facilitator, and collaborative problem-solver. Students reported that the experience created a student-centered climate, increased autonomy, supported cognitive/social/emotional capacities, improved math understanding, and fostered positive attitudes toward AI. They also identified barriers, including weak problem presentation, overly surface-level questions, mismatches with learning styles, technical issues, lack of interoperability, and the need for teacher facilitation. Overall, the study argues that GenAI can extend traditional teachable-agent designs, but effective classroom use still requires stronger pedagogical design, multimodal support, and human teacher involvement.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative classroom study with thematic analysis, observations, interviews, and open-ended surveys. It is empirically grounded, but it has no counterfactual, no randomized design, and no objective outcome estimates, so it meets only limited credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful benefits for engagement and perceived math learning, but it reports no measured effect sizes or direct achievement outcomes. Because the evidence is perceptual and descriptive, the practical impact remains unclear rather than demonstrably modest or large.

interventions.use_case: A generative AI-powered teachable agent for middle school mathematics, using GPT-4-Turbo in a chatbot-like interface to simulate a less knowledgeable peer that students teach while solving rate-and-ratio problems.

finding.finding_summary: This is a qualitative classroom study of 108 sixth-grade students, plus 14 interviewees, examining students’ perceptions of a GenAI-powered teachable agent in math. Students reported higher engagement, enjoyment, self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, and a more positive attitude toward math and AI, but these were self-reported perceptions rather than measured achievement gains. No counterfactual or effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Student perceptions from open-ended surveys, focus-group interviews, and classroom observations; themes on enjoyment, self-efficacy, motivation, and attitudes

finding.finding_summary: Students perceived the GenAI teachable agent as supporting cognitive, social, and emotional capacities, including elaboration, perspective-taking, communication skills, and resilience/growth mindset. The evidence is thematic and descriptive, not experimental, so no effect size or counterfactual comparison is available.
finding.measure: Perceived cognitive, social, and emotional capacity development from qualitative responses

finding.finding_summary: Students reported that teaching the GenAI-powered TA helped them better understand rate-and-ratio concepts and apply knowledge in new contexts. However, this paper does not report a direct achievement test, comparison group, or effect size; the evidence is limited to qualitative perceptions and classroom observations.
finding.measure: Perceived improvement in math subject-matter knowledge and application of knowledge in rate and ratio
